1.12. PARVOVIRUS

•Incubation period 4 – 14 days.
•DNA – virus single stranded DNA.
•Spontaneous replication in diving cells (S – phase).
•Replicate and inhibit CFU & cause lysis of human erythroid progenitor cells.

Transmission:

•Droplets borne:
-50 – 90% house hold contact.
-20 – 30% in school staff.

Out Breaks: in spring.

50% of child bearing are immune.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

•Vertical transmission 30% (so TOP not indicated).
•1% of susceptible individuals are infected /year, 1 infection /400 pregnancy, 23 times higher during epidemics.

Fetal risks:

•Loss rate 9% highest in 2nd .
•Hydrops 3% commonest finding (10 – 20% of non – immune hydrops).
•Reticulocytosis (> 20% Good prognostic sign)
•spontaneous recovery 34%
•IUD <10% after 4 – 6weeks.

Diagnosis:

•IgM (3 days – 6m0).
•Pregnancy + rash + arthralgia.
•Exposure history.
•Non – immune hydrops.
•IUD.

Counselling + decision to investigate.

•Serial USG for up to 12 weeks after confirmed infection.

Treatment:

•Maternal – symptomatic treatment.
•Hydrops – FMU referral.
•Delivery if Gestation is appropriate.
•FBS with conservative management if reticulocytosis positive.
•IUT if anemia on FBS

Transmission:

•< 15 weeks = 15%.
•15 – 20 weeks = 25%.
•Last = 70%.

Important facts about perinatal infections:

•Maculopapular rash on palms and soles and periostitis => syphilis.
•Hydrocephaly, Intracerebral calcification, chorioretinitis=> Toxoplasmosis treatment sulfadiazine + leucovorin.
•Cataract, SN deafness VSD, PDA, extramedullary hematopoiesis => rubella B/L hearing loss.
•Microcephaly, PV calcification, deafness Plt, petechia => CMV unilateral deafness treatment ganciclovir.

•Limb hypoplasia, cutaneous lesions => varicella.
•Still born + petechial rash = listeria.
•EONNS + maternal cheese intake = listeria.
•Most common cause of EONNS = GBS.
•2nd most common cause of EONNS= listeria.
•CMV transmission 1st & 2nd = 40%.
•CMV recent infection = low avidity.
•CMV infection = high avidity.
